subject.title: feat(agents): add iteration budget for agent loop safety

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the narrowed `maxToolCallingRounds` contract at default, subagent-default, and per-agent scope with mandatory tool-free closeout and built-in-harness-only enforcement?
rationale: This introduces a permanent public config surface and intentionally makes configured plugin-harness runs fail closed; implementation quality alone cannot decide whether those scope and compatibility semantics are the desired product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrowed contract
options.body: Adopt the single opt-in setting across the three scopes after the branch is rebased, the package boundary is fixed, tests are split, and current-contract live proof is supplied.

options.title: Pause for a generic harness contract
options.body: Hold this PR while maintainers decide whether tool-round limits must first become a supported generic harness capability rather than a built-in-only setting.

options.title: Keep existing safeguards only
options.body: Decline the new config surface and continue relying on targeted loop detection, run retries, abort handling, and issue-specific fixes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the single opt-in setting across the three scopes after the branch is rebased, the package boundary is fixed, tests are split, and current-contract live proof is supplied.
